title: Outlier-resistant quantile summarizer for inference KPIs
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Define and ship a memory-efficient, outlier-resistant streaming quantile summarizer to produce stable p50/p90/p99 estimates for per-tenant LLM inference KPIs across heterogeneous ingestion paths (OTel histograms, Prometheus buckets, and custom adaptor events). This component will live in the telemetry ingestion layer and provide both per-tenant and global summaries with explicit handling for bursty edge nodes and noisy tails.
background: Current latency SLI calculations rely on raw histogram buckets from various sources. We observe large variance from outliers and inconsistent bucketization across SDKs and edge proxies. This causes flapping SLO alerts and noisy dashboards for customers on Dedicated and Private deployments. Existing attempts to compute quantiles in the query layer (Prometheus / ClickHouse) are expensive or inaccurate when cardinality grows.
goals: Provide stable streaming quantile estimates (p50/p90/p95/p99) with bounded memory per tenant
Be resilient to short-lived outliers (e.g., noisy node, large cold-start spikes)
Support mixed inputs: OTLP histograms, Prometheus remote_write, and custom JSON metric envelopes
Expose summarizer outputs as Prom-compatible metrics and OTLP gauge/time-series for downstream SLO computation
Integrate trace hooks so quantile regressions can link back to span-level traces for debugging
non_goals: Replace long-term raw histogram retention or full-fidelity time-series storage
Perform offline reprocessing of historical data (out of scope for MVP)
proposed_solution: Build a streaming summarizer service implemented as a lightweight Go sidecar that attaches to the telemetry ingestion tier. Core algorithm will be a hybrid KLL + reservoir approach: KLL sketch for compressible distribution with a reservoir buffer for recent samples. Add an outlier dampening layer that employs a short-term median absolute deviation (MAD) score to downweight bursts. For OTLP histograms, convert buckets into representative samples before feeding the sketch with weight heuristics. For Prom remote_write we use bucket normalization and deterministic bucket-to-sample mapping to reduce bias. Summaries emitted at 10s and 1m granularity with labels: tenant_id, model_family, region, and quantile_type. Provide a compatibility path to export per-tenant quantiles back into Prometheus via a pushgateway-like endpoint and as OTLP metrics for consumers that prefer traces-native ingestion.
architecture_notes: The sidecar will accept incoming OTLP/Prom payloads, perform lightweight enrichment (tenant extraction, model tags), feed the summarizer sketch, and emit two productized outputs: (1) Prom metrics endpoint (pull) for scraping by Prometheus remotes and (2) OTLP/gRPC stream to the metrics bus for SLO calculation. The component will be horizontally sharded by tenant hash with sticky routing at the ingest layer. To avoid hot shards for large tenants, we implement tenant-scope fanout and per-tenant memory caps with graceful degradation (emit coarse quantiles and a marker label 'degraded=true').
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype summarizer algorithm (KLL+reservoir + MAD) with synthetic latency distributions
Week 2: Integrate prototype into otel-collector pipeline as a filter, add sample conversion for OTLP histograms and Prom buckets
Week 3: Build Go sidecar binary, add sharding and config (memory caps, emission intervals), unit & property tests
Week 4: End-to-end test with canary traffic (internal models) and compare against baseline Prom/ClickHouse quantiles
Week 5: Dashboarding, alert tuning, and rollout to a small customer cohort; collect feedback and iterate
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end quantile drift relative to ground-truth reservoir sampling < 2% for p50/p90/p95 under normal load
Under bursty outlier scenarios, p99 volatility reduced by >30% compared to current pipeline
Memory per tenant stays within configured cap; large tenants show 'degraded=true' and fall back to coarse-resolution summaries rather than OOM
Instrumented trace hooks link quantile spikes to 1-3 candidate spans in >70% of test cases
Expose metrics and dashboards for both 10s and 1m resolutions; internal canary customers see fewer false-positive SLO alerts over a 72h window
test_plan: Unit tests for sketch invariants, integration tests converting OTLP histograms and Prom buckets, chaos tests that inject node-level spikes and network partitions, and regression tests comparing quantiles against a ground-truth sample store using real traffic replay from staging. Load test to validate memory and CPU at 10K tenants and 100k events/s ingestion. Canary for 1 week on internal cluster before external customers.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy sidecar as opt-in feature flag behind telemetry-config; 2) Canary to internal-only tenants with 5% traffic; 3) Expand to low-risk external tenants (non-SLA) for 48h; 4) Promote to all tenants with burst-mode defaults; 5) Monitor dashboards and revert if regression (>5% increase in SLO misses) observed.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: 'Quantile Summaries by Tenant' (p50/p90/p95/p99), 'Sketch Health' (memory usage, merge error rate), 'Degraded Tenants' count. Alerts: sketch-memory-threshold, high-merge-error-rate (>0.5%), and quantile-drift-alert when per-tenant quantile deviates >5% from sample-ground-truth for >10min.
open_questions: What is the acceptable emission interval tradeoff for accuracy vs cost for tiered customers?
Should we persist per-tenant sketches for short warm restarts or rely on fast rehydration from recent buckets?
Do we add tenant-level SLA tiers that influence memory caps automatically?
risks: Sketch merge errors under heavy fan-in could bias quantiles if not properly normalized
Sticky sharding may create hot shards for very large tenants unless fanout is applied
Prometheus consumers may misunderstand approximate quantiles (documentation & labels required)
mitigations: Normalize weights during bucket-to-sample conversion and add merge sanity checks
Implement per-tenant fanout and eviction policy to avoid single-hot-shard OOM
Add explicit metric labels (approx=true) and documentation examples for SLO owners
notes: This approach aims to balance operational cost and downstream accuracy: approximate sketches reduce storage and query cost while providing stable SLO signals. The outlier dampening layer is experimental and will be feature-flagged. If successful, this component becomes the canonical source for quantiles used by alerts and cost-optimization signals.
